name: Venetoclax
route_note: oral tablets once daily with food, with a 5-week dose ramp-up in CLL to reduce tumour lysis
originator: AbbVie and Genentech (with the Walter and Eliza Hall Institute)

discovery.by: AbbVie (Andrew Souers and colleagues) with Genentech and WEHI
discovery.note: Re-engineered from navitoclax (ABT-263) to spare BCL-XL and so avoid dose-limiting thrombocytopenia.

tagline: First BCL-2 inhibitor: a BH3 mimetic that triggers apoptosis in leukaemia cells
summary: Venetoclax is a first-in-class oral BH3 mimetic that selectively inhibits the anti-apoptotic protein BCL-2, allowing cancer cells to undergo programmed cell death. It is used in chronic lymphocytic leukaemia, often as fixed-duration therapy with obinutuzumab or rituximab, and with hypomethylating agents or low-dose cytarabine for older or unfit patients with acute myeloid leukaemia.
mechanism: BCL-2 sequesters pro-apoptotic proteins such as BIM and prevents BAX/BAK from permeabilising mitochondria. CLL cells and many AML cells depend heavily on BCL-2 for survival.

Venetoclax binds the BH3-binding groove of BCL-2 with sub-nanomolar affinity, displacing BIM and triggering BAX/BAK activation, cytochrome c release and caspase-mediated apoptosis. Killing can be so rapid that tumour lysis syndrome is a major risk.
uses: Chronic lymphocytic leukaemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma (with obinutuzumab or rituximab, or alone)
Newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukaemia in adults ≥75 years or unfit for intensive chemotherapy (with azacitidine, decitabine or low-dose cytarabine)

history.title: BCL2 discovered
history.detail: BCL2 is identified at the t(14;18) breakpoint in follicular lymphoma; in 1988 it is shown to block cell death rather than drive proliferation.

history.title: ABT-199 reported
history.detail: Souers et al. (Nature Medicine) describe the BCL-2-selective inhibitor.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Accelerated approval for CLL with 17p deletion after at least one prior therapy.

history.title: MURANO and AML
history.detail: Approved with rituximab in relapsed CLL; accelerated approval in AML with azacitidine, decitabine or low-dose cytarabine.

history.title: CLL14
history.detail: Fixed-duration venetoclax plus obinutuzumab approved for untreated CLL.

history.title: VIALE-A
history.detail: Survival benefit with azacitidine leads to full approval in AML.

facts: The dose ramp-up (20, 50, 100, 200, 400 mg weekly) in CLL was introduced after fatal tumour lysis in early trials.
